recognize_zh: 組合圖中 A 為肉眼可見整片深紫色的骨髓抹片；B 高倍下背景為紫紅色無結構的顆粒狀壞死物，細胞輪廓模糊，只剩核固縮（pyknosis）的深染小核與鬼影細胞，形態無法判讀，符合骨髓壞死（bone marrow necrosis）。
features: Panel A: gross slide with an intensely dark purple, thick smear visible to the naked eye
Panel B: amorphous, granular eosinophilic-to-purple proteinaceous necrotic background replacing normal hematopoietic cells
Panel B: cells with indistinct borders, pyknotic hyperchromatic nuclei, and ghost-like outlines of red cells and nucleated cells
Panel C: low-power field with poorly preserved, pale smeared material and red cells, lacking identifiable marrow elements
Panel D: blood-diluted area with an arrowed small cell showing a pyknotic/fragmented nucleus; very few viable nucleated cells
describe_en: Composite figure of an iliac bone marrow aspirate. Grossly the smears are diffusely dark purple after May-Grunwald-Giemsa staining (A). Microscopically, the normal hematopoietic elements are replaced by an amorphous, granular eosinophilic-to-purple necrotic background containing ghost cells with indistinct borders and scattered pyknotic nuclei (B), with other fields showing poorly preserved material (C) and only rare degenerated cells with pyknotic or fragmented nuclei (D, arrow). Cell lineage cannot be assessed and no viable neoplastic population is identifiable on the aspirate. Findings are consistent with bone marrow necrosis; the underlying process (here a plasma cell neoplasm on biopsy) requires trephine biopsy and ancillary studies.

ddx.dx: Staining or fixation artifact (thick or poorly dried smear)
ddx.vs: Artifact affects cells uniformly but preserves identifiable nuclear and cytoplasmic detail, whereas necrosis shows pyknotic ghost cells in a granular proteinaceous background with necrosis confirmed on biopsy.
Gelatinous transformation shows a pink-purple, homogeneous mucoid ground substance with hypocellularity but no pyknotic ghost cells, and stains with Alcian blue.
Fibrosis yields a hypocellular dilute aspirate rather than necrotic debris, and the trephine shows reticulin/collagen fibrosis instead of coagulative necrosis.

ddx.dx: Diffuse marrow infiltration by acute leukemia or lymphoma with degeneration
ddx.vs: Viable blasts or lymphoma cells are identifiable in at least some fields or on biopsy, whereas here essentially no viable cells remain for morphologic or flow analysis.
